The "Organizational" topic in this corpus pertains to the structural distribution and involvement of practicing cardiologists ([[praktiserende-kardiologer|Praktiserende kardiologer]]) across different Danish regions. Understanding this organizational landscape is crucial for evaluating how specialist care is delivered and geographically distributed for incident patient pathways.

According to the data, a small group of 15 practicing cardiologists were involved in 5% of the incident patient pathways [^src1]. This highlights a concentrated level of specialist involvement in specific patient cases at the national or aggregate level.

Geographically, the organizational presence of practicing cardiologists varies significantly by region. The [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] has the highest concentration, with 13 specialist practices employing practicing cardiologists [^src2]. In contrast, the [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] has only 2 specialist practices with practicing cardiologists [^src2], and the [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] has just 1 specialist practice [^src2]. This disparity illustrates a heavily centralized organizational structure for private specialist cardiology in the capital area compared to the more rural regions.
